content: The Founder lifts the seedling out of the tin himself and puts it back in its paper cup. 'Pot, then. Keep the tin. Until your test says otherwise.' He reads Brand's sentence twice. 'A numbered object that grows. I can stand behind that. Draft, not final.'

decisions.text: PP7: working identity line 'A numbered object that grows' (draft); drop leads, plant is the reveal; guide advises sowing in a pot and keeping the tin until the tin-vs-pot test says otherwise; layered unboxing sequence adopted

content: Head of Product points at Research. 'A test for this one before we write it in stone. Cheap, please.'

Research has it ready. 'Two cuts of the same reel. Cut A opens on the number, the plant shows at the end. Cut B opens on the bloom, the number shows at the end. Same waitlist page, which also asks one question: who is this for, you or someone else? Then we can see which framing pulls which group, from real people, not my guesses about them.'

proposals.text: Framing test: Cut A (number first, plant reveal) vs Cut B (bloom first, number reveal); waitlist asks 'for you or for someone else?'
proposals.test: signups and self-reported buyer type per cut

content: Brand, half reluctant and half relieved: 'If Cut B wins I'll eat my words, on camera if Growth wants. But I'll shoot both properly. No sabotaging the one I don't like.'

The Designer redraws the lid card. The front now reads the number and 'a numbered object that grows'. The back has four grow steps that begin 'Sow in a small pot, keep the tin', followed by the remedy line.
The Plant Specialist gives the Founder a rare smile. 'If the tin turns out to work, I'll be the first to tell you, and you'll have a better story than anyone in this room could write.'
Growth holds out a fist to Brand. 'Two doors, one test. I'll build the waitlist page tonight.' After a beat, Brand bumps it.
Community watches the fist bump between Growth and Brand, an hour after their hook fight, and makes a mental note: this team argues hard and still lands somewhere.

CX reads the new card over the Designer's shoulder. 'Sow in a pot, keep the tin. If that had been in Archive 001, half my dead-seed thread might not exist. We'll never know, but it's the right sentence.'
Ops thinks it through: 'sow in a pot' means some buyers won't own a pot. Do we ship one? No. That would be a new SKU, more packing and more weight. They decide to say no before anyone asks.
Finance wonders if someone will propose shipping a pot. They'd have to price it, and they already know they'd argue against it.
Legal notes in the shared doc: 'Identity line is a brand statement, not a claim. Grow instructions must match test results. OK as drafted, subject to professional review of the final card.'
